note: Use the first form after a final consonant and the second after a vowel; do not insert a subject when context makes it unnecessary.
translation1: I am a student.
translation2: This place is a school.

note: The negative copula takes the subject particle on the noun being denied.
translation1: I am not a doctor.
translation2: This is not my bag.

english: as for N; topic or contrast
note: The topic particle introduces or contrasts a topic; it is not interchangeable with the subject particle in every context.
translation1: I live in Seoul.
translation2: As for coffee, I like it.

note: Choose the consonant-final or vowel-final form; new information and identification often use this particle.
translation1: It is raining.
translation2: A friend arrived.

note: Use after an object; it may be omitted in casual conversation but retain it in early controlled practice.
translation1: I read a book.
translation2: I drink water.

note: Existence and location use this particle; actions at a place normally use the action-location particle instead.
translation1: The book is on the desk.
translation2: I am not at home now.

english: at N; location of an action
note: Distinguish the place where an action occurs from a destination or location of existence.
translation1: I study at the library.
translation2: I eat lunch at a restaurant.

note: The particle marks a destination; the motion verb is chosen relative to the conversational viewpoint.
translation1: I go to school.
translation2: A friend comes to our house.

english: at N; time of an event
note: Used with clock times and many calendar expressions, but not normally with today, tomorrow, or yesterday.
translation1: Class starts at nine.
translation2: Let's meet on Monday.

note: The possessive particle is often omitted in speech; humble and familiar possessive pronouns have contracted forms.
translation1: This is a friend's book.
translation2: I know the name of the school.

note: The first is common in conversation; the latter pair is frequent in writing and more formal contexts.
translation1: I buy bread and milk.
translation2: I watch a movie with a friend.

note: This particle often replaces the subject or object particle; other combinations depend on the particle.
translation1: I am a student too.
translation2: I exercise today too.

note: Focuses on the noun; compare its scope with a negative sentence when interpreting restrictions.
translation1: I drink only water.
translation2: Only one friend came.

english: from N to N; starting and ending bounds
note: Useful with time; place-to-place routes also use a source-location particle.
translation1: I work from nine to five.
translation2: I go to school from Monday to Friday.

note: Use for a geographic starting point and endpoint.
translation1: I walk from home to school.
translation2: I go from Seoul to Busan by train.

note: Vowel harmony and common contractions determine the surface form; descriptive verbs do not need an extra copula.
translation1: I exercise every day.
translation2: The weather is nice today.

note: Choose by whether the stem ends in a vowel or consonant; stems ending in the liquid consonant need a deletion rule.
translation1: I learn Korean.
translation2: This room is quiet.

note: The past marker attaches to the stem before the polite ending; practice irregular stems as word families.
translation1: I met a friend yesterday.
translation2: I was very busy last week.

english: will; be going to; expected future
note: Expresses plans or predictions; avoid treating it as a mechanical equivalent of every English future.
translation1: I am going to read a book tomorrow.
translation2: I will rest on the weekend.

note: Direct statements usually concern the speaker; ask about the listener's wishes rather than asserting another person's internal state.
translation1: I want to go to Korea.
translation2: What would you like to eat?

note: Short negation; for many action nouns with the do-verb, place the negative immediately before the do-verb.
translation1: I am not going today.
translation2: This bag is not expensive.

note: Indicates inability or circumstances preventing an action, not simple unwillingness.
translation1: I cannot meet today.
translation2: I cannot swim.

note: Also has honorific statement uses; context and intonation distinguish requests from descriptions.
translation1: Please sit here.
translation2: Please read slowly.

note: Requests a helpful action; do not confuse the auxiliary with giving a physical object.
translation1: Please open the door.
translation2: Please say it again.

note: Attach the prohibition to the verb stem; this is not the ordinary negative statement form.
translation1: Please do not take photographs here.
translation2: Please do not speak too quickly.

note: Connects clauses without necessarily asserting a cause; tense is commonly expressed at the final predicate.
example1: 저는 책을 읽고 친구는 음악을 들어요.
translation1: I read a book, and my friend listens to music.
translation2: The room is big and clean.

note: Signals contrast between two clauses; it can attach after a tense marker.
translation1: It is expensive, but it is good.
translation2: I was busy yesterday, but today is fine.

note: At this stage teach ordinary explanations; avoid following the causal use with a command or suggestion.
translation1: I go to bed early because I am tired.
translation2: I am at home because it is raining.

english: go / come in order to V
note: The first predicate states the purpose of a motion verb; it is not a general-purpose replacement for all purpose clauses.
translation1: I am going to buy a book.
translation2: A friend came to eat.

english: shall we V?; shall I V?
note: A tentative proposal or offer; predictive question uses are introduced later.
translation1: Shall we have lunch together?
translation2: Shall I close the door?

note: Do not assume this ending is deferential enough for every request to a superior; a question may be more appropriate.
translation1: Let's study together.
translation2: Let's rest here for a little while.

note: Expresses ability or possibility; the bound noun is written separately.
translation1: I can read Korean.
translation2: I cannot go today.

note: Teach ongoing action first; resultant-state uses depend on the verb and are introduced later.
translation1: I am reading a book now.
translation2: I am waiting for a friend.

english: N that is A; descriptive noun modifier
note: Descriptive predicates directly modify nouns; the existential adjective family has a different modifier form.
translation1: I bought a small bag.
translation2: I have a good friend.

note: Use native or Sino-Korean numbers according to the counter; native one through four contract before counters.
translation1: Please give me two apples.
translation2: Three students came.

note: Honors the subject, not the listener; some common predicates use a special honorific word instead.
translation1: The teacher is reading a book.
translation2: Grandmother came.

english: may V; be allowed to V
note: Use a question to request permission; descriptive predicates are possible but not the central classroom use.
translation1: May I sit here?
translation2: You may leave early today.

english: must not V; V is not allowed
note: A conditional plus negative permission construction; it usually expresses a rule or warning.
translation1: You must not park here.
translation2: You must not talk during the test.

note: Expresses necessity; the second auxiliary is frequent in conversation.
translation1: I have to do the homework by tomorrow.
translation2: I need to go to the hospital.

note: In a request it invites a trial; past tense often describes experience.
translation1: Try on these clothes.
translation2: I have tried making kimchi.

note: Use a completed-action modifier before the bound temporal noun.
translation1: Take the medicine after eating.
translation2: Let's meet after class finishes.

note: The first verb is nominalized without a past marker even when the overall sentence describes the past.
translation1: I brush my teeth before sleeping.
translation2: I learned Korean before coming to Korea.

note: The ordinary simultaneous-action use normally has the same subject in both clauses.
translation1: I cook while listening to music.
translation2: We talked while walking.

note: A neutral condition; some contexts describe recurring events rather than hypothetical situations.
translation1: If you have time, please call me.
translation2: When spring comes, flowers bloom.

english: I wish; it would be good if
note: Uses a past-shaped form for a wish that need not refer to past time.
translation1: I hope the weather is nice tomorrow.
translation2: I wish I spoke Korean better.

note: Expresses intention or a developing situation; introduce first-person plans first.
translation1: I plan to travel during the vacation.
translation2: I intend to go to bed early today.

note: Unlike the basic causal ending, it can readily support a command or suggestion.
translation1: Since it is cold, please close the window.
translation2: Since we have time, shall we walk there?

note: A relatively explicit causal expression; do not imply that every occurrence has a negative result.
translation1: The roads are congested because of the rain.
example2: 내일 시험이 있기 때문에 공부해야 해요.
translation2: I have to study because there is a test tomorrow.

english: N that does / is doing V
note: The present action modifier differs from the descriptive-verb modifier.
translation1: The person going over there is my friend.
translation2: The book I am reading is interesting.

english: N that did / has done V
note: This action-verb modifier marks completed action; context determines whether English uses past or present perfect.
translation1: I called the friend I met yesterday.
translation2: Try the food I made.

english: N that will be / is to be V
note: Marks prospective, intended, or possible action rather than only chronological future.
translation1: I chose the clothes I will wear tomorrow.
translation2: I have many books to read.

note: Nominalizes a clause; distinguish grammatical nominalization from a concrete thing described by a relative clause.
translation1: I like walking.
translation2: Speaking in Korean is fun.

note: Often appears in activity labels and fixed evaluative constructions.
translation1: This chair is comfortable to sit on.
translation2: Getting up early is difficult.

note: Places the comparison standard before the particle; the degree word may be omitted.
translation1: Today is colder than yesterday.
translation2: The train is faster than the bus.

note: Use a comparison set and a superlative degree word; do not mechanically duplicate English articles.
translation1: Among fruits, I like apples the most.
translation2: Minsu is the tallest in our class.

english: by means of; toward; made of N
note: Use the vowel form after a vowel or the liquid final consonant; the sense depends on context.
translation1: I go to school by bus.
translation2: I made a box out of paper.

note: The first two are ordinary recipient forms; the honorific form respects the recipient, not necessarily the subject.
translation1: I sent a letter to a friend.
translation2: I asked the teacher a question.

english: do V for someone; humble benefactive
note: Use the humble auxiliary when the beneficiary is someone being honored; it does not honor the actor.
translation1: A friend helped me with my homework.
translation2: I opened the door for Grandmother.

english: nothing but N; only N with negation
note: Requires a negative predicate; scope differs from simply attaching the ordinary only-particle.
translation1: I have only one thousand won.
translation2: I slept only three hours yesterday.

note: Distributes an event or property over members of a set or intervals.
translation1: I exercise every weekend.
translation2: Food differs from country to country.

english: N or N; V or V
note: Choose noun or predicate coordination; the noun particle also has quantity and fallback senses taught later.
translation1: I drink tea or coffee.
translation2: On weekends I read books or watch movies.

note: Can confirm shared knowledge or soften a statement; do not use as a universal English question-tag replacement.
translation1: It is cold today, isn't it?
translation2: You are coming tomorrow too, right?

note: Expresses a newly noticed impression; distinguish surprise from a request for agreement.
translation1: Oh, this flower is pretty.
translation2: You speak Korean well, I see.

note: The modal depends on context; fixed polite expressions should be learned as complete social acts.
translation1: I will do it first.
translation2: You must be very tired.

note: Describes a decision or arrangement rather than merely a desire.
translation1: I agreed to study with a friend.
translation2: I decided to start exercising this month.

note: With descriptive stems, presents a change rather than a static property; passive uses require separate attention.
translation1: The weather has become warm.
translation2: Korean has become a little easier.

english: come to V; end up V-ing
note: Highlights a change in circumstances rather than a straightforward intentional act.
translation1: I have come to work in Seoul starting next month.
example2: 친구 덕분에 이 노래를 알게 됐어요.
translation2: Thanks to a friend, I came to know this song.

note: Emphasizes completion before the next activity.
translation1: I rested after finishing my homework.
translation2: I eat after washing my hands.

note: Action verbs take the present action form, descriptive verbs the descriptive form; existential predicates are a special family.
example1: 지금 공부하는데 조금 조용히 해 주세요.
translation1: I am studying now, so please be a little quiet.
translation2: This bag is pretty, but it is too expensive.

note: Select the modifier for predicate type and time; use it to mark an inference, not as empty filler.
translation1: It seems to be raining outside.
example2: 이 신발은 조금 작은 것 같아요.
translation2: I think these shoes are a little small.

note: Long-form inability combines with verb stems and can carry tense at the final auxiliary.
translation1: I could not rest because I was too busy.
translation2: I cannot read it because the print is small.

note: Long-form negation is useful in careful speech and writing; apply tense to the final auxiliary.
translation1: I do not eat meat.
translation2: This problem is not difficult.

english: report that V; indirect declarative quotation
note: Action-verb present quotation uses its declarative modifier; descriptive verbs and nouns use different quoted endings.
translation1: My friend said that they are coming tomorrow.
translation2: My younger sibling says they exercise every day.

english: report that something is A / N
note: Keep predicate-type distinctions rather than applying the action-verb quotation form to every predicate.
translation1: I heard that this restaurant serves good food.
translation2: They say that person is a doctor.

note: Quotation reports the content of a question, not its original politeness ending; longer question forms also occur.
translation1: My friend asked where I was going.
translation2: The teacher asked whether the problem was difficult.

english: tell someone to V; reported directive
note: Use the command quotation form, and identify who gave the instruction and who must act.
translation1: The doctor told me to rest well.
translation2: The teacher told us to read it by tomorrow.

english: suggest that we V; reported proposal
note: Reports an invitation or joint-action suggestion; it is not a direct command.
translation1: My friend suggested watching a movie together.
translation2: A colleague suggested having lunch early.

english: I should / will have to V
note: Usually conveys the speaker's newly formed judgment or resolve.
translation1: I feel ill, so I should rest.
translation2: There is no time, so I will have to take a taxi.

note: Describes experience on at least one occasion rather than the duration of an ongoing activity.
translation1: I have lived in Korea before.
translation2: I have never met that person.

english: do completely; end up doing irreversibly
note: Completion often carries relief, regret, or surprise; the emotional evaluation comes from context.
translation1: I ended up deleting the important file.
translation2: I finished all the homework that had piled up.

english: do and leave in the resulting state
note: Often used for preparation; some verbs use a more natural lexical expression instead.
translation1: I took out the clothes for tomorrow and left them ready.
translation2: I left the window open to air the room.

english: do in advance and keep the result
note: Overlaps with leaving a result in place but especially highlights preparation or preserving a useful state.
translation1: I wrote down the address for later.
translation2: Reserve the tickets before the trip.

note: Can describe simultaneous events with different subjects; nouns combine directly with the duration noun.
translation1: While I cooked, my younger sibling cleaned.
translation2: I read a book while waiting for the bus.

note: Typically switches from an ongoing action to another event; the first action is not necessarily completed.
translation1: I fell asleep while studying.
translation2: I met a friend while going home.

english: did V and then reversed / changed course
note: Marks completion before a contrasting or reversing subsequent action.
translation1: I opened the window, then closed it because it was cold.
translation2: I went to the store and then returned home.

note: Shows immediate succession; ordinarily the first clause does not take a separate past marker.
translation1: I showered as soon as I got home.
translation2: I will go to the library as soon as class ends.

note: A concessive relation where the second clause holds despite the first.
translation1: I will go even if it rains.
example2: 조금 비싸도 이 제품을 사고 싶어요.
translation2: I want to buy this product even if it is a little expensive.

note: Can describe repeated, current, or future situations; completed-time contexts may require a past marker.
translation1: I read when I have time.
translation2: I lived in the countryside when I was young.

note: Refers to elapsed time since an event; write the bound noun separately.
example1: 한국에 온 지 일 년이 됐어요.
translation1: It has been a year since I came to Korea.
example2: 점심을 먹은 지 두 시간 됐어요.
translation2: It has been two hours since I ate lunch.

english: because of doing V; negative consequence
note: Usually action verbs with the same subject, and an unwanted result; avoid commands in the result clause.
translation1: I could not sleep because I was doing homework.
translation2: I missed the explanation because I was answering the phone.

note: Normally introduces a favorable result; ironic negative use requires clear context.
translation1: Thanks to my friend's help, I finished the work.
translation2: Commuting is easy thanks to convenient transportation.

english: because of; owing to an unfavorable cause
note: Typically assigns an undesirable consequence to a cause; use carefully when blaming people.
translation1: I missed the train because I left late.
example2: 길이 미끄러운 탓에 차가 천천히 가요.
translation2: Cars are moving slowly because the road is slippery.

note: Inference from evidence; descriptive predicates commonly use the latter form.
example1: 밖에서 우산을 쓰네요. 비가 오나 봐요.
translation1: People outside are using umbrellas. It must be raining.
example2: 표가 다 팔린 걸 보니 인기가 많은가 봐요.
translation2: Seeing that the tickets sold out, it must be popular.

note: Marks uncertainty; avoid presenting the proposition as confirmed information.
translation1: It might rain tomorrow.
translation2: That rumor might not be true.

note: Usually past form for an event that nearly happened but did not.
translation1: I almost fell on the stairs.
translation2: I almost missed the flight because I overslept.

english: know / not know how to V
note: Skill and method use differs from the belief or expectation sense of this same construction.
translation1: I know how to ride a bicycle.
translation2: I do not know how to use this machine.

note: A periphrastic causative; permission versus compulsion depends on context and the participants.
translation1: The teacher had the students read the text.
translation2: I let the children play outside.

note: Passive suffix choice is lexical and must be learned with the verb; not every verb permits a suffix passive.
translation1: The door opened.
translation2: Music can be heard from far away.

note: Typically combines with suitable intransitive or passive predicates; contrast ongoing-action progressives.
translation1: The door is open.
translation2: The students are seated on chairs.

english: in an A way; adverbial manner
note: Converts a descriptive predicate into an adverbial; fixed lexical adverbs may be more idiomatic for some stems.
translation1: Please write the letters large.
translation2: I cleaned the room thoroughly.

note: Offers a measured characterization rather than an absolute claim.
translation1: I tend to go to bed early.
translation2: This neighborhood is relatively quiet.

note: Provides a purpose clause with a volitional action; the agent normally controls the intended action.
translation1: I went to the park to exercise.
translation2: I enrolled in this class to learn Korean.

note: Combines intention or confident expectation with a reason for the following request or judgment.
example1: 제가 요리할 테니까 설거지를 해 주세요.
translation1: I will cook, so please wash the dishes.
translation2: The roads will probably be congested, so let's leave early.

note: Can supply a concerned expectation or background; it need not always be translated as a direct contrast.
translation1: You must be tired, so get some rest.
example2: 지금쯤 집에 도착했을 텐데 연락이 없어요.
translation2: They should have arrived home by now, but there has been no message.

note: Use the adverbial form before a predicate and the modifier form before a noun.
translation1: I gave a presentation about Korean culture.
translation2: I am reading a book about the environment.

english: depending on N; according to N
note: Can mark variation by a condition or compliance with a rule; distinguish the two uses from context.
translation1: We will change the plan depending on the weather.
translation2: I installed the machine according to the instructions.

note: The noun construction is introduced first; clauses use a modifier plus the bound noun.
example1: 이곳은 학생뿐만 아니라 직장인도 많이 와요.
translation1: Not only students but also many office workers come here.
example2: 그 사람은 영어뿐만 아니라 한국어도 잘해요.
translation2: That person is good at Korean as well as English.

english: you know; as we both know
note: Invokes shared or supposedly shared knowledge; it can sound reproachful and should not be overused with strangers.
translation1: Today is Sunday, as you know.
translation2: I told you earlier, remember.

note: Reports a personal observation or discovery; restrictions on reporting one's own deliberate action require attention.
translation1: When I went there myself, I found there were many people.
translation2: I found the new book harder than expected.

english: N that used to / was V/A
note: Retrospective modifier often suggests ongoing, repeated, or uncompleted past experience; contrast the completed-past modifier.
example1: 예전에 자주 가던 카페가 문을 닫았어요.
translation1: The cafe I used to visit often has closed.
translation2: Where did you put the book I was reading?

english: N that had been / had V-ed
note: Usually looks back on a completed or bounded past situation; context can overlap with the simpler retrospective form.
translation1: I revisited the house where I lived last year.
translation2: The neighborhood that was once quiet has changed a lot.

english: I observed X, and then Y; contrasting observation
note: Normally links a remembered observation to a subsequent result or contrast; do not freely narrate one's own intentional action with it.
translation1: It was cold in the morning, but it became warm in the afternoon.
translation2: My younger sibling studied hard and then passed the exam.

english: when I did V, I found / got
note: Usually relates the speaker's completed action to a discovered result or response.
translation1: After I took the medicine, I felt a little better.
translation2: When I opened the door, a cat came in.

english: as I kept V-ing, I came to
note: An ongoing or repeated activity leads to a realization or outcome that was not the initial focus.
translation1: As I read every day, my reading speed increased.
example2: 친구와 이야기하다 보니 시간이 많이 지났어요.
translation2: As I talked with a friend, a lot of time passed.

note: Presents an expected result of continued action, unlike a retrospective result already reached.
translation1: If you keep practicing, you will get used to it.
example2: 여러 사람을 만나다 보면 생각이 달라질 수 있어요.
translation2: Meeting many people over time can change your views.

note: The degree or continuation of the first condition covaries with the second.
translation1: The more I learn, the more interesting it is.
translation2: The colder the weather, the fewer customers there are.

note: Contrasts two properties or situations, often within an analytical comparison.
example1: 이 집은 넓은 반면에 교통이 불편해요.
translation1: This home is spacious, whereas transportation is inconvenient.
example2: 형은 운동을 좋아하는 반면에 저는 독서를 좋아해요.
translation2: My older brother likes sports, whereas I like reading.

note: Can express substitution or compensation; the intended relation must be made clear.
translation1: I walked instead of taking a taxi.
translation2: The room is small, but the rent is low in compensation.

english: on top of; in addition to
note: Adds a further factor pointing in the same evaluative direction.
example1: 이 식당은 맛있는 데다가 가격도 싸요.
translation1: This restaurant's food is tasty, and the prices are low as well.
translation2: The roads are congested, and it is raining on top of that.

note: Concedes the first proposition before qualifying it; the nominalizer attaches before tense on the final predicate.
translation1: It is convenient, but it costs a lot.
translation2: I did go, but I did not stay long.

note: Often introduces a stronger hypothetical concession than a simple concessive connective.
translation1: Even if I fail, I will try again.
translation2: However busy you are, you should keep your promises.

note: Limits the assertion without the necessarily negative predicate required by the negative-only particle.
translation1: I merely stated the facts.
translation2: I am just a little tired.

note: Extends additive comparison to clauses; tense and modifier choice depend on the intended time.
example1: 그는 노래를 잘할 뿐만 아니라 춤도 잘 춰요.
translation1: He not only sings well but also dances well.
example2: 이 제도는 비용을 줄일 뿐만 아니라 시간도 절약해요.
translation2: This system not only reduces costs but also saves time.

english: while remaining in the state of V
note: Marks a maintained state during another action, not two independent ongoing actions.
translation1: I fell asleep with the light on.
translation2: Please do not come in with your shoes on.

english: because of an unexpected event; unfortunate result
note: Typically describes an unplanned event causing an undesirable outcome.
translation1: I was late because the bus unexpectedly arrived late.
example2: 컴퓨터가 고장 나는 바람에 일을 못 끝냈어요.
translation2: I could not finish the work because the computer broke down.

english: to the extent that; in proportion to; given that
note: The degree comparison and causal interpretation depend on context.
translation1: Your skill improves in proportion to how much you practice.
example2: 중요한 일인 만큼 신중하게 결정해야 해요.
translation2: Since this is an important matter, we must decide carefully.

note: Presents an outward display that differs from reality; modifiers follow predicate type.
translation1: Do not pretend not to know.
translation2: I pretended to be fine, but I was actually worried.

note: A calculation or interpretive conclusion rather than literal identity.
example1: 이 돈이면 한 달을 공짜로 쓰는 셈이에요.
translation1: At this price, it amounts to using it for one month free.
translation2: In effect, half is already finished.

english: also with the purpose of; killing two birds
note: Names one of multiple compatible purposes; a repeated construction can make both purposes explicit.
translation1: I walk to work partly to get some exercise.
example2: 책도 살 겸 친구도 만날 겸 시내에 갔어요.
translation2: I went downtown both to buy books and to meet a friend.

note: Contrasts an intention with a subsequent change before or during execution.
translation1: I was going to take the bus but took the subway instead.
translation2: I was about to call but decided not to because it was late.

english: if you intend / want to V
note: Specifies a prerequisite for an intended result or action.
example1: 이 일을 끝내려면 시간이 더 필요해요.
translation1: To finish this work, we need more time.
translation2: If you want to become healthy, you need to exercise regularly.

note: Motivates precautions through an uncertain feared outcome.
translation1: I left early because I was afraid I might be late.
translation2: I made a note because I was afraid I might forget.

english: there is no way; cannot possibly
note: Expresses the speaker's strong inference, not independently verified proof.
example1: 그 사람이 약속을 잊을 리가 없어요.
translation1: There is no way that person would forget the appointment.
translation2: It is so cheap that it cannot possibly be genuine.

note: Recognizes one possible outcome among alternatives; scope differs from simple ability.
translation1: The plan could change.
example2: 같은 말도 다르게 들릴 수 있어요.
translation2: The same words can sound different.

note: Often supplies information the listener may not know; repeated use can sound defensive.
example1: 오늘은 일찍 가야 해요. 가족 약속이 있거든요.
translation1: I need to leave early today. You see, I have a family appointment.
example2: 이 길로 가세요. 그쪽은 공사 중이거든요.
translation2: Take this road. The other way is under construction.

note: Conditional connective, distinct from the explanatory sentence ending; often followed by a request or suggestion.
translation1: If you have time, please contact me.
example2: 그 책을 다 읽거든 저에게 빌려주세요.
translation2: When you finish that book, please lend it to me.

english: just because; on the grounds that
note: With a negative conclusion, rejects an overgeneralization based on the quoted proposition.
example1: 비싸다고 해서 다 좋은 것은 아니에요.
translation1: Just because something is expensive does not mean it is good.
example2: 쉽다고 해서 준비를 안 하면 안 돼요.
translation2: You should not skip preparation just because it is easy.

note: Introduces remembered hearsay and often invites a response; distinguish personal evidence from quoted information.
example1: 그 영화가 재미있다고 하던데 같이 볼까요?
translation1: I heard that movie is interesting; shall we watch it together?
example2: 내일 비가 온다고 하던데 우산을 챙기세요.
translation2: I heard it will rain tomorrow, so take an umbrella.

english: so that; until; to an extent
note: Teach purpose or enabled outcome here; do not force every occurrence into a command meaning.
example1: 모두 들을 수 있도록 크게 말해 주세요.
translation1: Please speak loudly so everyone can hear.
translation2: Hurry so that you are not late.

english: make sure to; arrange for V
note: Common in instructions and self-commitments; strength depends on speaker roles and context.
translation1: Make sure to submit it by tomorrow.
translation2: I will make sure to be punctual from now on.

english: depending on whether / how one V
note: Embeds an indirect question before the variation construction; preserve the question's semantic focus.
translation1: The response varies depending on how you explain it.
translation2: The price differs depending on where you buy it.

note: Compares against a standard; unlike the ordinary comparative particle, it is especially useful in expository prose.
translation1: The number of visitors increased compared with last year.
translation2: The quality is good relative to the price.

note: Names the source of a claim; the tutor must not invent real studies or statistics to fill this pattern.
translation1: According to the notice, applications close today.
translation2: According to the weather forecast, it will be clear tomorrow.

note: Used in labels, concise records, and formal prose; not a replacement for every spoken nominalization.
translation1: We inform you that applications have closed.
translation2: I apologize for failing to keep my promise.

english: have no choice but to; necessarily
note: Expresses necessity from circumstances rather than a mere rule or preference.
example1: 자료가 부족해서 판단을 미룰 수밖에 없습니다.
translation1: We have no choice but to postpone judgment because the data are insufficient.
example2: 비용이 오르면 가격도 오를 수밖에 없어요.
translation2: If costs rise, prices inevitably have to rise too.

note: Presents a general tendency; avoid turning a stereotype into a supposedly universal rule.
translation1: Everyone naturally makes mistakes at first.
translation2: Problems are likely to arise when preparation is insufficient.

note: Highlights a controllable or varying factor that changes the result.
translation1: The outcome depends on how you prepare.
translation2: The same words can differ in meaning depending on how they are received.

english: it is generally the case; a principle
note: States a general principle, often with a didactic tone; distinguish from practical knowledge of how to do something.
translation1: As experience accumulates, one's perspective generally broadens.
translation2: It is the nature of people to change.

english: be worth V-ing; be reasonably A
note: The action evaluation and tolerability readings must be distinguished from ability.
translation1: This report is worth reading.
translation2: This amount of noise is tolerable.

english: to the extent that; enough to
note: Specifies degree by a result or benchmark, sometimes rhetorically rather than literally.
translation1: I was so nervous that my voice shook.
translation2: I explained it simply enough for anyone to understand.

english: as you can see / know; virtually
note: The basic connective points to an accessible fact; the auxiliary construction can mean practically or almost.
translation1: As you can see, all the seats are occupied.
translation2: As you know, this issue is not simple.

note: An approximate characterization, not an exact identity or a literal report of another person's speech.
translation1: I practically stayed up all night because of the deadline.
translation2: After hearing the news, I walked here almost at a run.

english: end up V-ing; regrettably / finally V
note: Marks an eventual outcome often contrary to hopes; emotional force varies with context.
translation1: I tried to hold back until the end, but I ended up crying.
translation2: In the end, we had to cancel the plan.

english: manage to V; bring V to completion
note: Emphasizes overcoming difficulty and achieving a result.
example1: 긴 협상 끝에 합의를 이끌어 냈습니다.
translation1: After lengthy negotiations, we managed to reach an agreement.
translation2: I managed to do the difficult work on my own.

note: Formal statement of purpose; appropriate for proposals and presentations rather than ordinary casual chat.
translation1: In this study, we seek to identify the cause.
translation2: We would like to hear the opinions of local residents.

note: A written causal connective, not the instrumental particle; select predicate inflection appropriately.
translation1: Since safety is important, the rules must be followed.
translation2: Because there are many applicants, registration closes early.

note: A nominalized action plus means marker, distinct from the similar-looking causal connective.
example1: 자료를 공개함으로써 신뢰를 높일 수 있습니다.
translation1: Trust can be increased by disclosing the data.
translation2: We found a new solution by discussing it together.

english: in V-ing; when it comes to V
note: Frames an area of relevance; avoid repetitive use when a simpler expression is clearer.
example1: 언어를 배우는 데 있어서 꾸준함이 중요합니다.
translation1: Consistency is important in learning a language.
example2: 정책을 평가하는 데 있어 자료의 질이 핵심입니다.
translation2: Data quality is central to evaluating policy.

note: A premise creates an obligation or logical consequence; distinguish this from the noun meaning above or more.
translation1: Now that you have promised, you must take responsibility.
translation2: Given that the problem has been confirmed, action is necessary.

note: Limits the claim to the stated condition or scope.
example1: 규칙을 지키는 한 누구나 참여할 수 있습니다.
translation1: Anyone may participate as long as they follow the rules.
example2: 제가 아는 한 그 소문은 사실이 아닙니다.
translation2: As far as I know, that rumor is not true.

note: Useful for parallel actions or contrasting aspects in expository writing.
example1: 시설을 확충하는 한편 직원 교육도 강화했습니다.
translation1: We expanded the facilities while also strengthening staff training.
example2: 편리한 한편 개인정보 보호 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
translation2: It is convenient, but privacy issues can arise.

note: Rejects an expected positive outcome and often introduces a worse or more basic failure.
translation1: Far from getting any rest, I did not even have time for lunch.
translation2: Far from helping, it actually got in the way.

english: let alone N; not even N
note: The noun version can compare a less attainable thing with a more basic unmet requirement.
translation1: Let alone taking a vacation, I work even on weekends.
translation2: There was not even an explanation, let alone an apology.

note: A reason used in narration and explanation; the evaluative use after an action has a different construction.
example1: 불이 켜져 있기에 누가 있는 줄 알았어요.
translation1: Because the light was on, I thought someone was there.
translation2: Since there were many questions, I added an explanation.

english: because I noticed; so I reacted
note: Conversational reason tied to the speaker's observation and response; do not make it an all-purpose formal causal connective.
example1: 사람들이 줄을 서 있길래 저도 기다렸어요.
translation1: I saw people lining up, so I waited too.
translation2: The price was low, so I bought two.

english: while at it; taking the opportunity
note: Uses an already planned or completed action as an opportunity for an additional action.
translation1: While I was downtown, I bought a book too.
translation2: Since we have started cleaning, let's clean the windows too.

english: if one is going to V, better to
note: The first option is dispreferred relative to the alternative; often strongly evaluative.
example1: 대충 할 바에야 시작하지 않는 게 낫겠어요.
translation1: Rather than do it carelessly, it would be better not to start.
example2: 계속 기다릴 바에야 다른 곳으로 갑시다.
translation2: Rather than keep waiting, let's go somewhere else.

english: merely; all one can do is
note: A restrained formal conclusion, often expressing regret, gratitude, or lack of alternatives.
translation1: All we can do is hope for a good result.
translation2: I can only express gratitude to those who helped.

english: after; at the end of a long process
note: Highlights a result reached through sustained activity or difficulty.
translation1: After lengthy discussions, we reached an agreement.
example2: 여러 번 시도한 끝에 문제를 해결했어요.
translation2: After several attempts, I solved the problem.

english: as soon as; in accordance with
note: Immediate succession with action verbs differs from following instructions or matching a manner.
translation1: I will let you know as soon as the results come out.
translation2: Write down exactly what you heard.

note: Marks alternatives, not retrospective recollection; distinguish its spelling and meaning from the retrospective ending.
translation1: Please let us know whether you will participate or not.
translation2: Wherever you live, health is important.

english: whether or not; regardless of another's action
note: Often sounds indifferent or dismissive; practice context and relational consequences.
example1: 사람들이 믿거나 말거나 사실은 변하지 않아요.
translation1: Whether people believe it or not, the facts do not change.
example2: 그가 듣거나 말거나 저는 설명을 계속했어요.
translation2: Whether he listened or not, I continued explaining.

note: A tentative intention; not the same as a firm plan or a fear construction.
translation1: I am thinking of applying online this time.
translation2: I am considering resting at home this weekend.

english: if it had been; if one had V-ed
note: Counterfactual past condition; the result often uses a modal or conditional evaluation.
example1: 조금 일찍 출발했더라면 기차를 탔을 거예요.
translation1: If I had left a little earlier, I would have caught the train.
example2: 자료를 확인했더라면 실수를 줄일 수 있었겠죠.
translation2: If we had checked the data, we could have reduced the mistakes.

english: should have V-ed, but did not
note: Retrospective unmet obligation or regret; state what actually happened when evaluating the meaning.
translation1: I should have reserved in advance, but I forgot.
example2: 그때 사실을 말했어야 했는데 그러지 못했어요.
translation2: I should have told the truth then, but I could not.

note: Reports an expectation that may be contradicted; distinguish from knowing how to perform an action.
translation1: I did not expect it to take this long.
example2: 금방 끝날 줄 알았는데 아직도 진행 중이에요.
translation2: I thought it would finish quickly, but it is still ongoing.

english: can be regarded as; may be said to
note: Useful for a qualified interpretation; it should be supported by evidence rather than merely sounding academic.
example1: 이 변화는 긍정적이라고 볼 수 있습니다.
translation1: This change can be regarded as positive.
example2: 두 요인이 함께 작용한다고 볼 수 있어요.
translation2: It can be said that the two factors operate together.

note: A corrective contrast; modifier form changes with predicate type and time.
example1: 비용을 줄이는 것이 아니라 사용 방식을 바꾸는 겁니다.
translation1: We are not reducing costs; we are changing how it is used.
example2: 관심이 없는 것이 아니라 시간이 부족한 거예요.
translation2: It is not that I am uninterested; I do not have enough time.

note: Introduces a representative member of a larger group; the list should support the generalization.
translation1: Residents participated as well as students.
example2: 서울을 비롯해 여러 도시에서 행사가 열립니다.
translation2: The event is held in several cities, including Seoul.

english: be no more than N; amount merely to N
note: Downscales an amount or status; use carefully because it may dismiss someone's contribution.
example1: 그것은 여러 가능성 중 하나에 불과합니다.
translation1: It is only one of several possibilities.
example2: 현재 결과는 예비 조사 결과에 불과해요.
translation2: The current results are merely preliminary survey results.

note: Formal or literary concession, often paired with a strong commitment in the next clause.
translation1: Even if I fail, I will uphold my principles.
translation2: Although progress may be slow, the direction is clear.

note: Concedes a less favorable condition while asserting a contrasting value; register is emphatic or literary.
translation1: The home may be small, but I feel at ease.
translation2: Though I have little experience, my enthusiasm is greater than anyone's.

english: even if; even though; rhetorical concession
note: Often combines with a rhetorical question or a claim that the condition makes no difference.
translation1: Even if we regret it now, what would change?
example2: 아무리 설명한들 들으려 하지 않으면 소용없어요.
translation2: However much you explain, it is useless if they will not listen.

note: A formal additive connective that frequently reinforces an argument.
example1: 이 제도는 효율적이거니와 비용도 적게 듭니다.
translation1: This system is efficient, and it also costs little.
translation2: He has extensive experience and is also careful in his judgment.

note: A literary concessive form; focus on recognition and register before productive use.
translation1: Spring has come, yet the wind is still cold.
example2: 여러 번 경고했건마는 아무도 귀를 기울이지 않았다.
translation2: Although warnings were given several times, no one listened.

english: if one continues V-ing; while V-ing
note: Literary reflection connecting sustained action to an emerging state or insight.
example1: 옛 편지를 읽노라면 그 시절이 떠오른다.
translation1: As I read old letters, those days come back to me.
translation2: As one walks along a forest path, the mind grows calm.

english: in the course of trying to; saying that one V-ed
note: A formal or literary explanation of effort; distinguish from reported command morphology.
translation1: I tried to do my best, but the result fell short.
translation2: I tried to hurry, yet I ended up late.

note: Emphasizes an outcome unexpected after the completed action.
example1: 그는 사실을 알고도 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
translation1: He knew the truth yet said nothing.
translation2: Even after resting enough, the fatigue did not go away.

note: Use the added vowel after a consonant-final stem except a liquid-final stem. The concessive reading contrasts knowledge or circumstances with behavior; distinguish it from neutral simultaneous action.
translation1: Although he is busy, he contacts his family every day.
translation2: Despite knowing the truth, they pretended not to know.

english: after doing; given that one has done
note: Often frames a condition judged incompatible with the next result, especially with negation.
translation1: It is hard to gain trust after breaking a promise.
example2: 사정을 모르고서는 쉽게 판단할 수 없어요.
translation2: You cannot judge easily without knowing the circumstances.

note: Negative prerequisite construction; the final clause often expresses impossibility.
example1: 직접 확인하지 않고서는 결론을 내릴 수 없습니다.
translation1: We cannot reach a conclusion without checking directly.
translation2: It is difficult to agree unless both sides make concessions.

english: only when; given that; rhetorical criticism
note: Can mark a necessary threshold or a reproachful condition; teach the two readings separately.
translation1: The misunderstanding was resolved only after we met in person.
translation2: With preparation this inadequate, how could we succeed?

english: even if one tries; it would be of little use
note: Often evaluates a proposed action as ineffective; do not use to discourage a learner's legitimate effort.
example1: 지금 서둘러 봤자 마지막 버스는 이미 떠났어요.
translation1: Even if we hurry now, the last bus has already left.
example2: 혼자 고민해 봤자 해결되지 않을 수 있어요.
translation2: Worrying about it alone may not solve it.

english: given that; if it is the case that
note: Formal or literary premise supporting a normative conclusion; chiefly a reading-recognition target.
example1: 책임을 맡았을진대 끝까지 최선을 다해야 합니다.
translation1: Having accepted responsibility, one should do one's best to the end.
example2: 배움이 목적일진대 질문을 두려워할 이유가 없습니다.
translation2: If learning is the goal, there is no reason to fear questions.

english: even if it means having to V
note: Accepts a possible sacrifice in order to maintain a priority; distinguish commitment from a prediction.
example1: 시간이 더 걸리는 한이 있더라도 정확히 확인하겠습니다.
translation1: Even if it takes longer, I will check accurately.
example2: 계획을 바꾸는 한이 있더라도 안전을 지켜야 합니다.
translation2: Even if it means changing the plan, we must ensure safety.

english: there is no need to go so far as to
note: Softens an extreme reaction without rejecting all action.
translation1: There is no need to go so far as to apologize for that.
example2: 작은 실수 하나로 계획을 포기할 것까지는 없습니다.
translation2: There is no need to abandon the plan over one small mistake.

english: treat it as; consider it as if
note: Adopts a practical or hypothetical accounting of an event, unlike stating that it actually amounts to something.
example1: 경험을 쌓은 셈 치고 다시 시작하겠습니다.
translation1: I will treat it as experience gained and start again.
example2: 하루 쉬는 셈 치고 천천히 둘러보세요.
translation2: Think of it as taking a day off and look around at leisure.

english: be barely at a threshold; consider whether to
note: Can express indecision with actions or approximation near a quantity; context resolves the meaning.
translation1: I hesitated over whether to participate and eventually applied.
example2: 회의에는 열 명이 될까 말까 한 사람들이 모였어요.
translation2: Barely ten people gathered for the meeting.

english: now that I consider V; if I choose V
note: A contemplated choice creates a problem; paired alternatives often express a dilemma.
example1: 집에 가자니 일이 남았고 더 있자니 너무 피곤해요.
translation1: If I go home, work remains; if I stay longer, I am too tired.
example2: 그냥 버리자니 아깝고 보관하자니 자리가 없어요.
translation2: It feels wasteful to discard it, but there is no space to keep it.

english: to think that; surprise at a proposition
note: A reaction to new or quoted information; it can express admiration, disappointment, or disbelief.
translation1: To think it is already finished; that was really fast.
translation2: It is surprising that you live so close.

english: I hear that; didn't you say that?
note: Checks reported or remembered information; intonation can make it sound accusatory.
translation1: I hear you are moving next month; is that right?
translation2: Didn't you say that reservations are not needed here?

english: if one keeps V-ing; warning of an outcome
note: A prospective undesirable outcome from continuing a behavior or condition.
example1: 그렇게 무리하다가는 건강을 해칠 수 있어요.
translation1: If you keep overworking like that, you could damage your health.
example2: 확인을 미루다가는 문제가 더 커질 수 있습니다.
translation2: If we keep postponing the check, the problem could become larger.

english: so that explains; linking a recollection to an explanation
note: A remembered observation is retrospectively explained; avoid confusing it with a simple hearsay statement.
translation1: So that explains why it was quiet: everyone had gone out.
translation2: So that explains the congestion: there was an event nearby.

note: A reasoned expectation rather than a rule or certainty.
translation1: With that much experience, it would be reasonable to expect proficiency.
translation2: Someone hearing it for the first time could understandably misinterpret it.

note: Literary or formal conjecture; normally less common than everyday inference constructions.
translation1: The negotiations seem likely to take longer than expected.
translation2: I suspect the outcome will be different this time.

english: almost; just on the verge of
note: A borderline or fluctuating perception, not a completed achievement.
example1: 멀리서 음악이 들릴 듯 말 듯 했어요.
translation1: Music was just barely audible in the distance.
example2: 기억이 날 듯 말 듯 해서 답답했어요.
translation2: It was frustrating because I could almost remember it.

english: the fact / matter that; as stated
note: Formal bound-noun reference; distinguish it from the immediate-discovery connective with similar spelling.
example1: 앞서 설명한 바와 같이 절차를 바꿨습니다.
translation1: As explained earlier, we changed the procedure.
translation2: Nothing has been confirmed so far.

note: A connective written attached to the predicate, unlike the bound noun meaning matter or fact.
translation1: Having reviewed the data, we find that further investigation is necessary.
example2: 본 사안은 공익과 관련되는바 신중한 판단이 요구됩니다.
translation2: Since this matter concerns the public interest, careful judgment is required.

note: Formal contrast; the bound noun here is spaced separately from the predicate modifier.
example1: 수요가 늘어나는 데 반해 공급은 줄고 있습니다.
translation1: Demand is increasing, whereas supply is decreasing.
example2: 목표는 분명한 데 반해 실행 계획은 모호합니다.
translation2: The goal is clear, whereas the implementation plan is vague.

english: as a consequence of N; owing to N
note: Formal cause, often describing a substantial consequence; avoid redundancy with another causal marker.
translation1: Operations were suspended owing to worsening weather.
example2: 그 결정으로 말미암아 여러 문제가 생겼습니다.
translation2: Several problems arose as a consequence of that decision.

english: regardless of N; irrespective of N
note: Generalizes across a named distinction; check that an inclusive claim is actually justified.
example1: 나이를 막론하고 누구나 배울 수 있습니다.
translation1: Anyone can learn, regardless of age.
translation2: Accurate information matters regardless of the field.

english: based on N; in accordance with a principle
note: Formal grounding in rules or principles rather than casual reliance on a source.
translation1: We must judge on the basis of evidence.
translation2: We designed the procedure based on the principle of fairness.

note: A scoped rebuttal that rejects a universal inference without asserting the opposite universally.
example1: 자료가 많다고 해서 반드시 결론이 정확한 것은 아닙니다.
translation1: Having much data does not necessarily mean the conclusion is accurate.
example2: 오래 일했다고 해서 반드시 성과가 좋은 것은 아니에요.
translation2: Working for a long time does not necessarily mean the results are good.

english: depend on whether / how; embedded question
note: Select the interrogative form for predicate type; the clause names the determining factor.
example1: 성공 여부는 얼마나 꾸준히 실천하느냐에 달려 있습니다.
translation1: Success depends on how consistently one puts it into practice.
example2: 해석은 어떤 맥락에서 사용되느냐에 달려 있어요.
translation2: The interpretation depends on the context in which it is used.

note: Calibrates epistemic certainty; follow with the specific missing evidence or alternative explanation.
example1: 이 결과만으로 효과가 없다고 단정할 수 없습니다.
translation1: We cannot conclude from this result alone that there is no effect.
example2: 한 번의 실수로 능력이 부족하다고 단정할 수는 없어요.
translation2: We cannot conclude from one mistake that someone lacks ability.

english: the reason / explanation for X is Y
note: A focus construction for explicit causal argument; avoid claiming causation when the evidence shows only association.
example1: 참여가 늘어난 것은 절차가 간단해졌기 때문입니다.
translation1: Participation increased because the procedure became simpler.
example2: 판단을 보류하는 것은 자료가 충분하지 않기 때문입니다.
translation2: The reason we are withholding judgment is that the data are insufficient.
